affected_job_families_and_configurations: Standalone simulator configurations with learning_setting=task_il and class_pair_protocol=strict; rejection only.
new_findings.description: Strict Task-IL singleton rejection message did not match the documented validation contract.
Non-stream arrival events populated class_id but omitted class_ids, although downstream event preparation sorts on class_ids; this caused KeyError during supported simulator execution.
affected_job_families_and_configurations: Standalone simulator configurations using non-stream arrivals across supported methods.

new_findings.description: EWC/MAS importance consolidation used global seen-class IDs as output coordinates for a task-conditioned head, causing invalid class indexing when class IDs exceeded the active task-head width.
affected_job_families_and_configurations: Task-IL simulator configurations using EWC or MAS with active task heads.
verification_evidence: .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/test_class_indexed.py -k importance or ewc or mas: 2 passed.

new_findings.description: An offline-client regression assertion expected a full replay archive under the selected-client archive download policy. The policy correctly delivers only to selected clients; the stale assertion contradicted the implemented recipient contract.
affected_job_families_and_configurations: Standalone selected-client archive policy with partial participation.
verification_evidence: The test now checks private classes remain local and received_memory is empty for the offline client; focused 12-test run passed.

new_findings.description: The frozen v16 factorial snapshot retained fingerprints and rejected-job example IDs from the pre-migration Class-IL registry after full_matrix.base changed to strict Task-IL. Feasible counts, family counts, accepted/rejected totals, and method/aggregator coverage remained identical.
affected_job_families_and_configurations: CIFAR-100 v16 full factorial registry, ViT and CNN.
verification_evidence: Compared all generated model fields; only hashes differed. Compared feasibility audit; counts and reasons were identical and only example job IDs differed. Refreshed only those fields. Validator passes with 32,133 feasible jobs per model, 99 method/aggregator pairs, 53,805 inputs, 21,672 rejected.

new_findings.description: The factorial validator retained outdated primary-probe expectations of one client worker and nine training intervals, while current primary_probe.py and docs define concurrency five and twenty intervals.
Primary-probe tests asserted retired V23 names, obsolete summary field layout, and old server-barrier wording despite current V27 Task-IL implementation.

Task-IL GEM/A-GEM reference-gradient extraction forwarded only the valid unpadded examples through the feature extractor, unlike the configured full physical training batch. With batch-dependent normalization, this made the reference gradient use different batch statistics from the physical-batch contract; padding was already excluded from the loss.
affected_job_families_and_configurations: Task-IL GEM/A-GEM reference gradients using a final partial reference batch and batch-dependent model layers.
verification_evidence: .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/test_exact_batch_v16.py and combined affected tests passed; full repository suite passed with 458 tests and 335 subtests.

new_findings.description: Server-fidelity integration tests used the legacy synthetic disjoint schedule, which created singleton Task-IL tasks and failed before reaching the aggregation, offline exposure, acknowledgement, or hidden-index assertions. The fixtures now allocate all synthetic labels to both clients under a stationary scenario, producing valid multi-class Task-IL tasks while preserving distinct client sample indices.
affected_job_families_and_configurations: Synthetic server aggregation and client acknowledgement integration tests.
verification_evidence: .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/test_server_fidelity_v11.py: 16 passed; full repository suite passed with 458 tests and 335 subtests.

new_findings.description: Two Task-IL paths mishandled task-local output semantics: spurious reversed-test evaluation omitted independent task IDs and indexed local head columns as global classes; synthetic label noise selected from the full global label space and could produce targets outside the originating head.
affected_job_families_and_configurations: Task-IL synthetic/domain label-noise runs using task-conditioned heads.
verification_evidence: .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/test_expanded.py passed in the full suite; full repository suite passed with 458 tests and 335 subtests.

new_findings.description: Both scheduling paths remain single-host. The joint broker schedules local GPU IDs with node-local flock leases; the authoritative 152-slot diagnostic run_suite uses a local ThreadPoolExecutor, local output-root locks and local subprocesses. Current tests cover local exclusive leases and GPU gates, but do not establish cross-host atomic claims, coordinator restart recovery, stale-worker reconciliation, or collision-free attempt directories across Mtech and V100.
affected_job_families_and_configurations: All jobs scheduled concurrently or recoverably across Mtech and V100.
regression_test_coverage: No cross-host diagnostic_campaign runner test is present.
new_findings.required_correction: Implement or configure a coordinator with verified cross-host atomic claims, per-attempt identity and output isolation, durable controller recovery, resource reservations, stale-worker reconciliation, and checksum-verified artifacts; inject controller and worker failures across both hosts before production admission.
verification_evidence: Static inspection shows both run_suite and run_broker schedule local subprocesses and local GPU indices; no two-host coordinator integration or restart test was found in the repository test suite.
The 2026-11-28 release gate remains closed pending this work.
